findings.reason: a control that cannot redden the suite leaves §10's gate unable to show the retired write is gone, which is the whole measure §10 exists to assert.
findings.text: §10's done-when asserts "the contract harness … refuses a terminal `set`, so a surviving example fails it" and names as its negative control restoring the archive example's `set` of `status` that the contract test "then fails naming skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md"; that harness only fails an op the store refuses *for its path* — `_refusal_is_for_path` (tests/test_skill_contracts.py:2035-2043) matches three alternatives — `unsupported (plan|index) (set path|append target)`, `is (computed|counted) from`, `is not authorable` (`_REFUSAL_FOR_PATH`, tests/test_skill_contracts.py:2028-2032) — so a refusal that instead names `close`, which is what §6 specifies (line 189), is read as benign and the loop breaks on the first non-path refusal, leaving the test green; §10's write paths exclude tests/test_skill_contracts.py, so its node cannot widen the predicate within its fence

findings.reason: without the scope named, a node implementing the refusal over the shared `set` path either breaks the documented sprint close or must invent the exemption, and if it is exempted, `skills/reckon-sprint/SKILL.md` belongs in §10's fence.
findings.text: §6 retires the terminal `set status` for every resource ("a `set` of `status` to any value in `TERMINAL_STATUSES` is refused, naming `close`") but the only closure verb it adds is plan-scoped ("A plan closes in one write", line 168), while `skills/reckon-sprint/SKILL.md:188` documents `edit_plan(… doc_type="sprint", ops=[{"op": "set", "path": "status", "value": "done"}])` — the same write, for a sprint, which `close` does not cover and which no node's fence reaches (§6 writes `reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/_store_section_ops.py`, `reckon/mcp.py` and its tests; §10 writes five documents and no sprint file); the status handler already separates the two resources (`_apply_sprint_status`, `reckon/_store.py:2521`), so the scope is decidable — but unstated it decides the outcome of the sprint close path, and §10's own rationale ("any document still showing that write … teaches a refused op", line 252) applies to the file that would be left teaching it

findings.reason: the split stands on §10 owning the documents either way; an uncited figure weakens the rationale but does not redirect any node.
findings.text: §10 justifies the split with a measurement the plan does not cite: "§6's node needed 234,819 input tokens against the local lane's 230,144-token window", with no log, run id or revision named, so a later reader cannot check the figure and cannot tell whether it still holds after the fence changes it grounds

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — every file, section and commit §6 and §10 name resolves (`tests/test_terminal_status_needs_every_section_ticked.py`, `…every_section_has_a_declaration.py`, `…closure_gates.py`, `…continuation.py`, `…edit_plan.py`, `skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md:636`, the four reference files, the census doc that carries the 17/27 refusal counts), but §10's Why states a token measurement with no citation.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §10's done-when names a negative control (restore the archive example's terminal `set`) that cannot fire against the harness it names.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both changed units route their gate through repository test files and the landed evidence record at `docs/evidence/archive/every-plan-write-goes-through-edit-plan-landed.html#s6`, and neither writes a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `close` and the guard names, the section titles and the changed head metas carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6's claim that a terminal `set status` refusal is safe "because every reckon caller that sets one moves to `close`" leaves the sprint close path out of account.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 carries one deliverable (a plan closes in one write through `close`, with `set status` retired for terminal values), and §10 one (the five documents describe `close` and drop the retired instructions).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the head meta is extended correctly for the split (`s9←s6`, `s10←s6`, `s4←s2,s3; s5←s4; s6←s5; s7←s6; s8←s7`), all targets resolve and every transitive ordering §10 and §9 need is declared, but §6's terminal-`set` refusal is given no resource scope, so its reach over the sprint close path is unstated.
